10. Despite a popular backronym suggesting that this sport was an acronym for "■●♡♤□♤♡□♡□♡♡♡□♡♡□♡□" its true origins are far more linguistically humble and inclusive. The name likely stems from the Middle Dutch word "☆☆☆☆," meaning a club, which migrated across the North Sea to the shores of Scotland. Early royal advocates like Mary, Queen of Scots, helped transform this stick-and-ball pastime into the prestigious game played on "links" today. What is the four-letter name of this sport?

11. While history books frequently credit an Italian polymath for the 1609 invention of the device that brought the heavens closer to Earth, he merely refined an existing design. A year prior, a Dutch spectacle-maker named Hans Lippershey applied for a patent for a "looker" that used a combination of convex and concave lenses. Though the Italian improved the magnification and made the first significant astronomical discoveries, the Dutch inventor is the one who truly birthed the instrument. What is the name of this optical tool?

A public confrontation in 1770 resulted in the deaths of five civilians at the hands of British regulars, an event that was immediately seized upon by Paul Revere and other patriots for propaganda purposes. While the loss of life was tragic, the label applied to the event suggested a slaughter of hundreds, a narrative choice designed to galvanize a revolution against the Crown. This "bloodbath" branding worked so well that the minor skirmish is still taught in history books under this hyperbolic title. What is the two-word name of this event?
